name_in_paper: gene-level analysis of Affymetrix exon microarrays

evidence.quote: We assessed the innate immune response to MRKAd5/HIV by profiling transcriptomes of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) isolated from seven Ad5 nAb seronegative individuals (Ad5 nAb titer ≤18; Ad5Neg) during the first week after vaccination, by gene-level analysis of Affymetrix exon microarrays.
We used a modular analysis framework (21) to interpret the transcriptional response.
We confirmed the functional annotations of the gene modules themselves by performing canonical pathway enrichment analysis (Dataset S1, tab 3).

First, we quantified and confirmed the differential expression of mRNAs associated with several vaccine-regulated modules, including “Interferon response” [C-X-C motif chemokine 10 (CXCL10), ISG-15, and STAT1] (Fig. 1C).

Next, we corroborated the differential expression of many cytokines and chemokines at the protein level using multiplex serum analyte analysis (Fig. 1D and Dataset S1, tab 6), detecting robust changes in serum levels of IP-10, I-TAC, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), and MCP-2, as well as immunoregulatory IL-10 and IL-1Ra.

name_in_paper: directly assessing circulating peripheral blood leukocyte concentrations

evidence.quote: Finally, we validated the cellular trafficking responses predicted from the modular analysis by directly assessing circulating peripheral blood leukocyte concentrations (Fig. 1E and Dataset S1, tab 7), confirming vaccine-induced influx of monocytes and pronounced efflux of lymphocyte populations (T, B, and NK cells).

We therefore extended our analysis of the MRKAd5-induced innate response to the exon-level to further enrich our understanding of the action of the vaccine, with the primary focus of identifying vaccine-regulated genes not already detected by the gene-level analysis, particularly those behaving concordantly in vitro and in vivo.

Additionally, alternative transcription analysis identified 16 genes with vaccine-induced responses that varied strongly from exon to exon, but were nevertheless consistent in vitro and in vivo, including FANCA, FARP2, RERE, GBP6, and GBP7 (Fig. 2C and Dataset S1, tab 10).
We performed interaction network analysis to determine whether the genes commonly regulated by MRKAd5 in vitro and in vivo constituted established pathways or represented isolated nodes.
Finally, we validated these transcriptional results at the protein level by analyzing serum analytes from a larger set of vaccinated subjects (Fig. S2).
The predictive potential of individual cytokines and all cytokine pairs was evaluated by 60 iterations of eightfold cross-validation of linear discriminant analysis (LDA) classifiers.
Genes with statistically significant differences in vaccine-induced transcriptional responses between the high and low CD8+ groups were then identified through direct comparison.

name_in_paper: Agilent SurePrint G3 Human GE 8 × 60K microarray platform

evidence.quote: RNA from the MRKAd5 vs. YF-17D comparative in vitro study was analyzed using the Agilent SurePrint G3 Human GE 8 × 60K microarray platform (Agilent Technologies), essentially as described in ref. 17.

Serum cytokine analysis was performed using the Lincoplex High Sensitivity kit (Millipore Cat# HSCYTO-60SPMX13) and regular sensitivity kits (Millipore Cat# MPXHCYTO60KPMX42, MPXHCYP2:00 PMX23, and MPXHCYP3-PMX9), according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Linco/Millipore), and samples were analyzed on a Luminex 200 (Luminex).

name_in_paper: Enumeration and Phenotyping of Fresh Blood Cell Populations

evidence.quote: For further phenotyping, whole blood was diluted 1:10 in Pharm-lyse RBC lysis buffer (BD), incubated 10 min at room temperature and centrifuged at 750 × g for 5 min.
Cells were fixed with PBS containing 1% paraformaldehyde and stored at 4 °C until analysis by flow cytometry.
One-million PBMC from healthy Ad5-seronegative individuals were stimulated with MRKAd5 empty vector or GTS buffer mock control (60) or YF-17D or DMEM with 2% (vol/vol) FCS mock control.
